judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale:
The paragraph is the English translation of the 'Revisitar Amanhãs' exhibition summary, in the #weekExhibition list. In the crawler rendering Rampa received, this is indeed an English

with no lang attribute under , so the claim is literally true of that document. The site sniffs the user agent: HeadlessChrome, crawler, curl and Lynx user agents get an unstyled SEO/crawler rendering (no stylesheets, meta robots, every CMS field dumped with its Portuguese and English translation), while Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari user agents get a proof-of-work challenge and then the real styled page. Rampa's snapshot matches the crawler rendering exactly. I solved the challenge and fetched the real page on 2026-10-24: it is lang="pt" and entirely in Portuguese, and this English text does not appear in it at all (English lives on the separate /en page). A user in a mainstream browser with assistive technology never receives this passage, so on the page as users get it there is no unmarked English passage and no 3.1.2 failure. The finding comes from the collector being served a bot-only variant. If one chose to count the crawler rendering (also reached by Lynx) as user-facing, it would be a real 3.1.2 failure.

The site sniffs the user agent: HeadlessChrome, crawler, curl and Lynx user agents get an unstyled SEO/crawler rendering (no stylesheets, meta robots, every CMS field dumped with its Portuguese and English translation), while Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari user agents get a proof-of-work challenge and then the real styled page. I solved the challenge and fetched the real page on 2026-10-24: it is lang="pt" and entirely in Portuguese, and it has no 'É parte de' heading or these field-label headings at all. So the heading does not exist on the page users get. Even within the crawler rendering, 'Is part of' does describe the purpose of its section (the parent the event belongs to); what is missing is the content under it (an image with no alt, a 1.1.1 matter), so it would not be a clear 2.4.6 failure either.
